routes.reason: Core horizon, eye-level, parallel-line, and one-point explanations reinforce D’Amelio; Norling’s “high-water mark” earns only a teaching patch.
Reverse-engineering vanishing points and eye level from an existing image is a new operational capability.
Locating VPs/eye level and distortion from narrow spacing mostly duplicate the D’Amelio construction and distortion cards.
The paired-VP rotation model materially reframes the existing orientation Pattern but does not warrant a new card.
Bricks/city, scale placement, composition/interiors, diagonal centers, and spacing are strong reinforcement of existing D’Amelio cards.
Cylinder/ellipse material mostly overlaps D’Amelio; one ellipse-axis mnemonic is held as questionable pending later source verification.
Surface division reinforces plane metrology; shadow examples add a useful receiving-surface transition patch to the existing shadow AP.
Constructed level-plane reflections are absent from the cumulative baseline and earn a new Pattern.
Up/down convergence is already represented; the slope “false eye-level” is retained as a practical inclined-plane patch.
Mechanical/architect’s projection from plan and elevation is an exact workflow not represented by D’Amelio and earns an AP.

rationale: Norling behaves exactly as the second book in a cumulative curriculum should: the majority is Review/reinforcement, five deltas improve existing cards, three capabilities survive as new candidates, and one simplification is explicitly held for later verification. No whole-book Deep PASS is warranted.
